event_overview.title: About Gaza Conflict
event_overview.subject: Gaza Conflict
event_overview.summary: The Gaza Conflict refers here to the war and continuing violence involving Israel, Hamas and other Palestinian armed groups that followed the 7 October 2023 attacks from Gaza into Israel and Israel’s subsequent military campaign in the Gaza Strip. A ceasefire took effect on 10 October 2025 and ended large-scale hostilities, but United Nations reporting as of 21 November 2026 described continued Israeli strikes, shooting and shelling, Palestinian casualties, access restrictions and severe humanitarian needs in Gaza.

facts.label: Start and current status
facts.value: The present war began on 7 October 2023, when Palestinian armed groups from Gaza attacked communities and military sites in southern Israel and Israel began strikes on Gaza. A ceasefire effective 10 October 2025 ended large-scale hostilities but did not end violence.

facts.label: Location and principal parties
facts.value: The core theatre is the Gaza Strip and nearby areas of Israel. The conflict involves Israeli forces and Hamas alongside other Palestinian armed groups; civilians in Gaza and Israel have been directly affected.

facts.label: Pre-war context
facts.value: The United Nations describes Gaza as having been under an Israeli blockade of varying intensity since 2007, with recurrent escalations between Israeli forces and Palestinian armed groups before the 2023 war.

facts.label: Humanitarian and diplomatic framework
facts.value: UN Security Council Resolution 2728, adopted on 25 March 2024, demanded a Ramadan ceasefire leading to a lasting sustainable ceasefire, release of hostages, humanitarian access and compliance with international law. The 2025 ceasefire was supported by mediation involving Egypt, Qatar, Türkiye and the United States.

facts.label: International legal proceedings
facts.value: South Africa instituted proceedings against Israel at the International Court of Justice on 29 December 2023 under the Genocide Convention. The Court has issued provisional-measures orders; these are interim directions and do not decide the case’s final merits.
